audit: COLDWAR VIE structure, pacing and decision design

findings.title: Chinh's ten-step programme cannot fit the default historical mandate
findings.evidence: The shortest compatible route to the handover costs 665 nominal focus-days across ten completed focuses. The installed historical observer installs Chinh on 14 July 1986 and Linh on 18 December: 157 days. All Chinh focuses require Chinh personally, cancel when invalid and cannot continue under Linh.
findings.consequence: Only two seventy-day focuses fit the default historical window; its handover capstone is inaccessible in that window.
findings.qualification: An early alternate Chinh mandate can last longer. This is not a claim that every alternate history blocks his tree.

findings.title: All campaign forks are behind forced dual-lane introductions
findings.evidence: These are the only three multiple-block AND joins in the entire tree. Each requires a root, both two-focus lanes and the central join. Their minimum costs are respectively 420/385/385 focus-days and 0.095/0.100/0.100 billion in contributions.
findings.consequence: The first operational choice appears after more than a year of uninterrupted selections. The parallel-looking introductions are both compulsory.
findings.qualification: These are structural lower bounds before war/party/treasury waiting and other national priorities.

findings.title: The wartime defence and offensive bonuses arrive after lengthy war-only research
findings.evidence: Even with all earlier institutions prepared, China Crisis needs 35 days during actual CHI war before Hold can begin its 70 days. Hold's defensive bonus therefore arrives no earlier than 105 days into that response; Depth requires another 70. Phnom Penh Objective likewise needs 70 days of actual CBD war. cancel_if_invalid=yes and continue_if_invalid=no are emitted.
findings.consequence: A short real war can finish before the intended campaign bonus is granted. A focus-day standard designed for national institutions has become a reaction delay on operational orders.
findings.qualification: The script arithmetic is confirmed. Historical short-offensive dates are contextual and should be supplied by the historical research audit; no war duration or engine cancellation was simulated.

findings.title: Paid temporary policies expire while unlocking their own next layer
findings.evidence: The two guerrilla preparation lanes grant 180-day policies. Local replaces Cadres within liaison; Staff replaces Training within training. The lane completed first must wait at least three further seventy-day completions before Networks: its latest policy is expired by then. Survey, Command, Hold and Depth also replace one china_posture family rather than accumulating.
findings.consequence: Focus cards read like permanent institutional development, but several are paid replacement programmes whose useful window is consumed by the next focus chain.
findings.qualification: Replacement is intentional and correctly guarded; this is a pacing and presentation mismatch, not a claim of stacking bugs.

findings.title: Cambodia's limited route still points into a victory-only continuation
findings.evidence: Aftermath has Monitor OR Capital as focus prerequisites, but its live gate requires a real won Cambodian campaign. A limited peaceful route must instead use the separate x56 bypass and verified terms before the regional continuation.
findings.consequence: The central connector promises a continuation that the intended limited outcome normally cannot take.
findings.qualification: The bypass already prevents a total dead end. Do not award military victory merely to repair a drawing.

findings.title: Permanent locks sometimes separate complementary activities
findings.evidence: Front pressure excludes Paris talks; mobilisation excludes a diplomatic opening. Aircrew Training has only the Fleet parent, while Coastal Defence permanently excludes Fleet.
findings.consequence: Coercive diplomacy is prohibited and a coastal-defence choice unexpectedly forbids pilot training. These are unnecessary policy restrictions rather than asymmetric syntax.

findings.title: Fourteen different subjects share one sixteen-node template
findings.evidence: Nine political islands and five common branches each contain sixteen nodes over ten rows, three binary exclusive pairs and repeated OR reconvergence. A selected terminal route normally takes ten focuses. Alternating one/two-column offsets changes the silhouette slightly but not the repeated grammar.
findings.consequence: Distinct leaders, institutions, civilian sectors and military services read as interchangeable ten-step checklists.
findings.qualification: Native Russia is also very wide. Width and a grid are not intrinsically incorrect MD style.

findings.title: Outlook advocacy looks like ideology selection but unlocks no party tree
findings.evidence: All four outlook cards follow the civic root, have no mutual exclusions and can be completed sequentially. Exact-party/leader roots are independently gated and require none of those cards.
findings.consequence: The drawing invites an ideology-branch interpretation while the reward is a popularity/outlook intervention. Adding another mandatory outlook-unlock ceremony would worsen the issue.
findings.qualification: Permanent outlook exclusivity would conflict with the requested multiplayer party departure/return system; advocacy should be moved to decisions rather than made a permanent ideological prison.

findings.title: The civilian transition is a three-card preparation ceremony
findings.evidence: The three successive seventy-day cards all require the military-junta government. They grant programme modifiers and unlock flags; the civilian decision is a funded timed idea. Actual native political transfer remains separate.
findings.consequence: The labels promise a regime-level outcome while the tree remains under the old government's gate throughout.
findings.qualification: Do not repair this with a forced coup, automatic election winner or invented historical leader. Use a real player-owned native transition contract.

findings.title: Orderly islands have too little thematic hierarchy
findings.evidence: Political roots are at x12,20,...76 with the same ten-row height. The junta root is 6144 grid pixels right of the initial Duan root. Eighteen branch shortcuts already exist. The repeated grid is stronger than the thematic distinction between short-lived incumbents and permanent national systems.
findings.consequence: Shorten and differentiate leadership footprints, retain shortcuts and reserve space for genuine institutional forks. Do not compress titlebars onto adjacent columns.
findings.qualification: Source-bound overlap and structural checks are separate from native rendering; no game screenshot or conditional-hide refresh was tested.

recommendations.title: Make Chinh a two-focus congress mandate
recommendations.change: Keep the root plus one substantive exclusive seventy-day mandate. Move hearings, drafting and subsidy review into decision/event options. Remove the handover as a ten-step capstone; native succession remains authoritative.
recommendations.benefit: A 140-day route fits the 157-day historical window. An early alternate mandate can open additional decisions rather than another identical full tree.
recommendations.preserve: Remembered progress, genuine native succession and the distinction between personal active modifiers and lasting reforms.

recommendations.title: Move four outlook advocacy cards out of the focus spine
recommendations.change: Keep After Ho Chi Minh as the civic root. Make outlook advocacy native political decisions. Connect Cadres and Mass Organisation directly to state_root. Keep exact-party roots independent.
recommendations.benefit: Four ceremonial cards disappear; the shortest civic route loses seventy days without preventing future party changes.
recommendations.preserve: Party programme departure/reactivation follows actual power, not a permanently selected outlook focus.

recommendations.title: Make guerrilla preparation a genuine institutional choice
recommendations.change: Use political organisation versus professional small-unit schools as the first institutional fork. Move Local/Staff upgrades to paid programme decisions. Networks takes one OR group rather than requiring both lanes.
recommendations.benefit: A three-focus entrance costs 210 days before the operational choice, rather than 420. A later voluntary integration project can reward players who fund both capabilities.
recommendations.preserve: No fabricated units or universal rebellion. Rebalance programme terms and migrate old prerequisite flags together.

recommendations.title: Prepare Chinese defence before war and activate it during the real campaign
recommendations.change: Keep seventy-day defensive institutions and contingency planning available before war. Leave talks/rights optional. Crisis needs Northern Command, not both lanes. A gated paid war decision/event activates the chosen 180-day operational posture when an actual war begins; a long focus is not the sole way to issue an urgent order.
recommendations.benefit: Removes 140 mandatory preparation days and avoids waiting 105 days into a short war for the first defence bonus without breaking the seventy-day focus standard.
recommendations.preserve: Actual CHI combat gates, the user-approved entrenchment/core/forest/jungle values, family replacement, cost, expiry and hidden-tech cleanup.

recommendations.title: Give Cambodia separate diplomacy and military entrances
recommendations.change: Let commission requests start from the question/logistics institution without first needing Cambodian war or a hostile war goal. Make civilian protection optional. Merge frontier/command preparation. Mandate accepts real military preparation OR a genuinely accepted limited-security framework. Prepare an operational plan in a seventy-day focus, then activate its timed campaign effects with a real-war decision.
recommendations.benefit: Avoids a 385-day two-lane toll and lets diplomacy begin before a hostile crisis. The capital-campaign bonus need not wait seventy actual war days.
recommendations.preserve: A regime-change war goal still requires grave actual hostility. A commission never awards military victory, annexation or automatic peace.

recommendations.title: Clean up the limited Cambodia bypass
recommendations.change: Remove Monitor from the victory-node prerequisite. Merge Sovereign Border and Limited Commitment into one implementation focus; keep the actual limited review as a paid decision. Join the regional process from that verified limited node.
recommendations.benefit: One misleading connector and a repeated seventy-day/0.020-billion step disappear.
recommendations.preserve: Actual peace, no occupation, reciprocal drawdown, current terms and the separate limited verification. Saved flags need migration.

recommendations.title: Remove the paid Long Commitment acknowledgement
recommendations.change: The burden already follows actual occupation/native assistance. Remove the compulsory seventy-day/0.020-billion acknowledgement; offer exit policy after either administration branch.
recommendations.benefit: The player pays and waits for a policy, rather than for acknowledgement that the commitment exists.
recommendations.preserve: Offers remove no burden; verified withdrawal and actual mission termination stay authoritative.

recommendations.title: Do not permanently exclude diplomacy from military readiness
recommendations.change: Remove Pressure/Paris and Mobilisation/Opening permanent exclusions. Separate negotiation and military-programme families. Retain real force-structure incompatibilities and recipient consent.
recommendations.benefit: Supports fighting and negotiating, refusal and revised terms in multiplayer.
recommendations.preserve: Removing a focus lock alone is insufficient if the supposedly parallel ideas still silently replace one shared family.

recommendations.title: Detach Aircrew Training from the fleet choice
recommendations.change: Connect Aircrew Training to the shared service institution or an independent air branch. Reserve Coastal/Fleet exclusivity for naval force structure.
recommendations.benefit: A coastal doctrine no longer forbids unrelated pilot training.
recommendations.preserve: Dockyards remain funded queued construction; no free aircraft or units.

recommendations.title: Replace the civilian-handover ceremony with a real transition contract
recommendations.change: Keep one mandate-setting focus, then negotiate the constituent timetable through native political events and decisions. Merge Assembly/Regular Mandate into that settlement rather than requiring another 140 days under the old government gate.
recommendations.benefit: The selected route changes permitted governing arrangements and lasting civic guarantees rather than merely unlocking another generic timed administration idea.
recommendations.preserve: No forced election winner or invented coup leader. Constitutional guarantees owned by the national settlement must not disappear merely because the old junta programme deactivates.

new_choice_pairs.title: The congress inherits a concrete economic mandate

left.label: Secure the Consumption Floor
left.advantage: Protect rations, wages and administrative continuity.
left.cost: Higher funded support burden and slower price adjustment.
left.follow_up: A finite emergency subsidy budget with actual paid tranches.

right.label: Release the Enterprises
right.advantage: Retained earnings and local procurement experiments.
right.cost: Temporary price/stability disruption and a smaller guaranteed consumption floor.
right.follow_up: Choose which real pilot programmes receive scarce funds.

new_choice_pairs.contract: Root plus choice is 140 days; hearings and handover are decisions/native succession. The congress settlement persists beyond Chinh, while his personal programme still follows office.
new_choice_pairs.position_status: replacement slots after associated merges; not a rendered replacement tree

new_choice_pairs.title: Le Duan allocates scarce national effort

left.label: Rebuild the North First
left.advantage: Commit the next programme to repair capacity and civilian output.
left.cost: Reduced operational mobilisation commitment during reconstruction.
left.follow_up: Choose actual paid northern construction/investment projects.

right.label: Sustain the Southern Effort
right.advantage: Protect military readiness and resources allocated to the real southern effort.
right.cost: Delayed civilian repair and consumption commitments.
right.follow_up: Choose a bounded real-war support programme without free units.

new_choice_pairs.contract: Rename the introductory mandate accordingly. Both routes may negotiate. Exclusive national allocation, not willingness to talk, is the incompatibility; later integration follows a real outcome.
new_choice_pairs.position_status: replacement slots after associated merges; not a rendered replacement tree

new_choice_pairs.title: Renovation deals with the cadre network

left.label: Negotiate a Cadre Compact
left.advantage: Preserve administrative continuity and provincial cooperation.
left.cost: Retained patronage costs and slower managerial accountability.
left.follow_up: Negotiate performance obligations with native personnel institutions.

right.label: Give the Auditors Authority
right.advantage: Reduce protected procurement and managerial abuses.
right.cost: Funded inspections and temporary political cohesion costs.
right.follow_up: Choose an audit target and accept a finite backlash, not an invented universal purge.

new_choice_pairs.contract: Both are party-led reform paths with different personnel and programme consequences. Constitutional pluralism is a separately negotiated governing transition rather than a generic research-bonus card.
new_choice_pairs.position_status: replacement slots after associated merges; not a rendered replacement tree

new_choice_pairs.title: A constitutional government settles wartime property claims

left.label: A Restitution Commission
left.advantage: Credible individual claims and civil property guarantees.
left.cost: Slow administrative resolution and disputes with current beneficiaries.
left.follow_up: Fund case-by-case claims and choose protections for current households.

right.label: A Compensation Fund
right.advantage: Settle claims without indiscriminate eviction or production disruption.
right.cost: A defined treasury contribution and longer public payment burden.
right.follow_up: Select an actually funded tranche with concrete numeric event effects.

new_choice_pairs.contract: Move foreign alignment to diplomacy. The settlement method creates different domestic obligations; it does not automatically transfer population, provinces or factories.
new_choice_pairs.position_status: replacement slots after associated merges; not a rendered replacement tree

new_choice_pairs.title: A military government chooses a credible civilian exit

left.label: Set a Constituent Deadline
left.advantage: A clear and rapid civilian constitutional mandate.
left.cost: Immediate uncertainty and reduced military appointment control.
left.follow_up: Negotiate actual native election/assembly guarantees with the player retaining political choice.

right.label: A Phased Civilian Cabinet
right.advantage: Administrative/security continuity during a staged transfer.
right.cost: Longer transition costs and weaker immediate civilian legitimacy.
right.follow_up: Fund milestones and permit reviewed failure or renegotiation.

new_choice_pairs.contract: Retain the existing permanent-council route. Within the chosen civilian-transition path, these are two viable transfer mechanisms with different obligations. The accepted result must reach the actual native political system, not only a timed buff.
new_choice_pairs.position_status: replacement slots after associated merges; not a rendered replacement tree

new_choice_pairs.title: The frontier army chooses an enduring force structure

left.label: A Fortified Border Zone
left.advantage: Prepared positions, entrenchment and homeland defence.
left.cost: Lower offensive flexibility and higher fixed personnel commitments.
left.follow_up: Fund defensive renewals; terrain training follows the active paid idea.

right.label: A Rotational Frontier Army
right.advantage: Rest, training cycles and a mobile reserve.
right.cost: Lower maximum prepared defence and repeated rotation costs.
right.follow_up: Choose funded schedules while retaining readiness during talks.

new_choice_pairs.contract: Diplomacy remains independently available with actual consent. Permanent institutional design differs from temporary operating programmes; retain expiry and family ownership, with no new CHI-only scalar defence needed.
new_choice_pairs.position_status: replacement slots after associated merges; not a rendered replacement tree

limits: No compiler or runtime/test runner was executed. Only layout.md and layout.json in this review directory were written.
Loaded focus AST, actual localization, actual effects/triggers and current main MD references are the evidence. Immutable design JSON identifies group membership, never final modifier values.

Nominal focus-days equal cost times seven, before external duration modifiers, treasury/party/war waiting and other priorities. Structural histories enforce focus grouping and exclusions, not every live condition.
Source geometry is not a native screenshot. Connector routing, clipping, hide/refresh behaviour, save behaviour and multiplayer balance remain untested.

The six pairs are replacement concepts, not twelve new mandatory cards. Their slot positions reuse removed forks after redesign and are not a rendered proposed tree. Exact modifier values/APIs need separate mechanics review.
Event implementation must show agreed costs/rewards as concrete numeric native option effects, with short English descriptions.

nodes.label: After Ho Chi Minh
nodes.description: Ho Chi Minh's death has left the revolution with a shared legacy and several centres of authority. Le Duan, President Ton Duc Thang and Prime Minister Pham Van Dong must hold the institutions together through another difficult year.
nodes.available_code: COLDWAR_VIE_is_1970 = yes

nodes.label: Defend the Revolution
nodes.description: The revolution survives through confidence in its purpose as well as organisation. Renew the argument for socialist construction and the struggle for national reunification.

nodes.label: Constitutional Debate
nodes.description: A constitution can be discussed even where an independent opposition cannot yet govern. Open a debate about public authority, legal protection and the terms of a future political settlement.

nodes.label: Broaden the Front
nodes.description: The Fatherland Front brings together organisations whose interests extend beyond the Party apparatus. Give those constituencies a greater voice in national affairs.

nodes.label: National Sovereignty
nodes.description: Independence remains the strongest common language of Vietnamese politics. Appeal to those who place sovereignty and the republic above competing ideological camps.

nodes.label: Professional Cadres
nodes.description: Administrative competence cannot be supplied by revolutionary credentials alone. Train cadres to investigate conditions, keep reliable accounts and deliver public services.

nodes.label: Mass Organisation
nodes.description: Mass organisations connect the state to villages, factories and neighbourhoods. Deepen that network while accepting the work required to maintain it.

nodes.label: Rural Schools
nodes.description: War has displaced teachers and disrupted schooling without extinguishing the ambition to learn. Extend education beyond the better served towns and protect the next generation of technicians.

nodes.label: Women in Public Life
nodes.description: Women sustain production, public administration and family life under exceptional pressure. Wider participation must be accompanied by practical support rather than another unpaid obligation.

nodes.label: National Assembly
nodes.description: The National Assembly can become a more useful channel between policy and the people who live with it. Strengthening its work requires an administration capable of responding.

nodes.label: Cadre Discipline
nodes.description: The cadre service must answer to a common chain of authority. Tighter discipline can improve execution, but it can also discourage honest disagreement.

nodes.label: Public Criticism
nodes.description: Policy failures do not disappear when nobody dares to describe them. Protect criticism that exposes abuse while accepting a more contested political environment.

nodes.label: Provincial Councils
nodes.description: Provincial authorities know local shortages and productive possibilities better than distant offices. Give their councils a clearer place in the national programme.

nodes.label: Freedom of Worship
nodes.description: Buddhist and Catholic communities are part of the nation, not a single political bloc. Negotiate practical protections for religious life and equal treatment before public authorities.

nodes.label: A Durable Charter
nodes.description: A durable charter must outlast the ambitions of its authors. Establish institutions that can carry public responsibilities through changes of leadership and government.

nodes.label: Southern Priority
nodes.description: Le Duan places the struggle in the South at the centre of national strategy. The North must sustain that effort while living with the demands it makes on reconstruction.

nodes.label: General Offensive
nodes.description: A concentrated offensive promises to change the balance of the war. It also requires a heavier logistical effort and a willingness to expose the main force to risk.

nodes.label: Protracted Pressure
nodes.description: Protracted pressure preserves the capacity to continue when a quick decision is impossible. Its discipline comes at the cost of postponing the victory many have been promised.

nodes.label: The Main Force
nodes.description: Bring the principal formations and their supporting production into a more concentrated effort. Farms and civilian workshops will feel the diversion of scarce resources.

nodes.label: Fight and Negotiate
nodes.description: Military pressure and negotiation can serve the same strategy. Prepare a diplomatic channel without assuming that the opposing governments will accept our terms.

nodes.label: The Party Congress
nodes.description: Peace permits a congress to turn from the endurance of war to the shape of the national economy. The ambitions adopted here must still confront limited resources and administrative capacity.

nodes.label: Heavy Industry First
nodes.description: Heavy industry promises greater national strength and a more independent military supply base. Giving it priority leaves fewer resources for the food economy.

nodes.label: Balanced Recovery
nodes.description: Recovery must feed the population as well as expand industry. Adopt a more balanced allocation even if it slows the growth of military production.

nodes.label: Industrial Combine
nodes.description: The northeastern industrial base can support a wider range of national production. Organise the planning and construction of a new combine rather than relying indefinitely on imported capacity.

nodes.label: Food and Goods
nodes.description: Food supply and everyday goods determine whether recovery is felt outside the offices of the plan. Direct more of the programme towards those immediate needs.

nodes.label: Integration Policy
nodes.description: The institutions of North and South cannot be joined by a proclamation alone. Where the country has actually been reunited, decide how quickly their administrations and economic arrangements should converge.

nodes.label: Rapid Transformation
nodes.description: Rapid socialist transformation offers a clear political direction for the newly integrated economy. Its pace risks disruption where existing production and distribution cannot adjust.

nodes.label: Gradual Transition
nodes.description: A gradual transition can preserve working enterprises and local knowledge. It asks the revolutionary leadership to tolerate arrangements that do not yet match its final objectives.

nodes.label: Collective Mastery
nodes.description: Collective mastery places organised labour and state institutions at the centre of production. Making it effective requires more than slogans and additional administrative offices.

nodes.label: Household Incentives
nodes.description: Household incentives can relieve pressure on food production without abandoning the socialist state. Such flexibility tests the authority of officials accustomed to uniform targets.

nodes.label: Socialist Unity
nodes.description: A unified socialist state must demonstrate that victory can become a sustainable civil order. Its social commitments will remain a claim on national resources.

nodes.label: Reassess the Plan
nodes.description: Truong Chinh's authority rests on long service and the power of political doctrine. The plan must now be examined against the conditions it has actually produced.

nodes.label: Planning Discipline
nodes.description: Planning failures can be answered with firmer discipline and clearer obligations. That approach preserves central authority while narrowing the room for local initiative.

nodes.label: Evidence before Dogma
nodes.description: Economic evidence should be permitted to challenge established formulas. Send officials to learn why production and distribution fall short of their instructions.

nodes.label: Procurement Targets
nodes.description: Binding procurement targets offer the state more predictable deliveries. They can also weaken the incentive to produce beyond what households need for themselves.

nodes.label: Provincial Inquiries
nodes.description: A provincial inquiry must listen to producers rather than merely confirm reports already written in Hanoi. Its findings may reveal useful experiments and uncomfortable failures.

nodes.label: Congress Documents
nodes.description: The congress documents must acknowledge the gap between intention and result. Prepare a reassessment that can give national renovation an intellectual and political foundation.

nodes.label: Retain the Subsidies
nodes.description: State subsidies protect expectations built over many years. Preserving them can cushion insecurity while committing the budget to continuing support.

nodes.label: Enterprise Autonomy
nodes.description: Enterprise managers cannot be held responsible for results if every practical choice requires distant approval. Grant more autonomy and accept the uncertainty of restructuring.

nodes.label: Ration Guarantees
nodes.description: Ration entitlements are a promise between the state and households under strain. Defending that promise must not conceal the weaknesses of the supply system behind it.

nodes.label: Selective Price Reform
nodes.description: Selective price changes can reduce distortions without attempting every reform at once. Households and enterprises will still face a difficult adjustment.

nodes.label: Party Rectification
nodes.description: Rectification should uncover administrative failure as well as punish misconduct. Honest review threatens networks that have learned to protect themselves.

nodes.label: Ideological Guardians
nodes.description: Ideological guardianship can preserve a common political direction. It risks turning a necessary reassessment into another exercise in obedience.

nodes.label: Prepare Renovation
nodes.description: Renovation requires permission to reconsider policies once presented as settled doctrine. Build that permission into the preparations for the next national programme.

nodes.label: Party Schools
nodes.description: Party schools should prepare officials to administer real institutions. Their expansion requires teachers, facilities and the resources of a sustained education programme.

nodes.label: Hear the Economists
nodes.description: Economists and technical specialists can identify constraints that political instruction alone cannot overcome. Give their arguments a serious hearing within the leadership.

nodes.label: An Orderly Handover
nodes.description: A handover can preserve continuity without denying the need for a new programme. Consult the existing leadership institutions and prepare an orderly succession.

nodes.label: Party Led Renovation
nodes.description: Nguyen Van Linh presents renovation as a task of the Party itself. Economic change must confront entrenched interests without dissolving the authority expected to carry it through.

nodes.label: Household Production
nodes.description: Household responsibility can connect effort more directly to the harvest. Make family production the principal instrument of agrarian renovation.

nodes.label: Collective Production
nodes.description: The cooperative form need not remain unchanged to survive. Retain collective production while revising its management, obligations and access to inputs.

nodes.label: Expand Rural Trade
nodes.description: Expand the circulation of rural goods so that a productive harvest can reach buyers. Wider commodity trade also exposes households to movements in the market.

nodes.label: Tools and Credit
nodes.description: Tools, credit and shared equipment can make cooperative reform tangible. Their provision is a continuing commitment rather than a substitute for better incentives.

nodes.label: Enterprise Accounts
nodes.description: State enterprises need accounts that reveal costs and responsibilities. Begin separating an enterprise's productive performance from its access to political protection.

nodes.label: Sequence Price Reform
nodes.description: Price reform can be sequenced so that institutions have time to adjust. A slower transition places a heavier burden on coordination and supervision.

nodes.label: End Blanket Subsidies
nodes.description: Blanket subsidies can no longer be treated as an unlimited promise. Their abrupt removal will expose enterprises and households to a painful transition.

nodes.label: A Consumption Floor
nodes.description: Renovation needs a floor beneath those least able to absorb its costs. Protect basic consumption even where doing so slows fiscal adjustment.

nodes.label: Fiscal Stabilisation
nodes.description: Expansion without fiscal restraint risks reproducing the instability reform was meant to address. Accept a period of tighter spending and slower growth while restoring order.

nodes.label: Necessary Action Now
nodes.description: Public criticism of abuse must reach beyond ceremonial self criticism. Expose practices that obstruct reform, even when influential cadres would prefer silence.

nodes.label: Party Monopoly
nodes.description: Economic renovation can proceed under a continued Party monopoly. Preserve that political boundary while changing the way the economy is managed.

nodes.label: Political Pluralism
nodes.description: Independent political organisation goes beyond consultation through the Front. Negotiate a new boundary of authority and accept a more fundamental challenge to the existing order.

nodes.label: Screen Foreign Capital
nodes.description: Foreign investment can operate under legal guarantees while remaining subject to state screening. That system preserves administrative control at the price of heavier supervision.

nodes.label: Investment Access
nodes.description: Broaden access to investment under clear legal safeguards. Greater openness promises new opportunities while increasing exposure to international conditions.

nodes.label: Renovation in Crisis
nodes.description: The socialist world cannot be assumed to remain a permanent source of support. Adapt renovation to a future in which Vietnam must rely on a wider range of economic relationships.

nodes.label: Experiment First
nodes.description: Vo Van Kiet's proposed national mandate puts practical administration ahead of rigid procedure. Begin with experiments that can demonstrate how production and distribution might work better.

nodes.label: Provincial Initiative
nodes.description: Provincial initiative can solve problems before a national rule is ready. It also reduces the centre's control over the path of reform.

nodes.label: A National Pilot
nodes.description: A coordinated national pilot can produce more comparable results. It requires a stronger apparatus to select projects, supervise them and evaluate their progress.

nodes.label: Goods for the Cities
nodes.description: Food and manufactured goods must be able to move from producers to the cities. Remove practical obstacles without pretending that wider circulation is free of market risk.

nodes.label: Project Delivery
nodes.description: Give priority projects an office responsible for delivery rather than another set of targets. Coordination itself must remain accountable for the resources it uses.

nodes.label: Power for Workshops
nodes.description: Reliable electricity determines whether workshops can make use of their labour and machinery. Prepare a period appropriate power project for the northern economy.

nodes.label: Retained Earnings
nodes.description: Enterprises should be able to retain enough earnings to repair equipment and respond to demand. That freedom changes the balance between managers and central allocation.

nodes.label: Priority Projects
nodes.description: Treasury support can keep essential projects from being abandoned between institutions. Concentration on selected works leaves fewer resources for other uses.

nodes.label: Local Supplier Networks
nodes.description: Local suppliers can reduce delays and connect workshops to a wider productive network. Give their development a place in the construction programme.

nodes.label: Northern Road Spine
nodes.description: A working road spine binds production to distribution. Organise the recovery of northern links that have become an obstacle to everyday economic life.

nodes.label: Named Responsibility
nodes.description: Responsibility should remain attached to a named office when a project fails. Auditing delivery challenges administrative practices that benefit from ambiguity.

nodes.label: Export Experiments
nodes.description: Small export experiments can test how Vietnamese producers meet outside demand. They also bring international fluctuations closer to the domestic economy.

nodes.label: Domestic Supply Chains
nodes.description: A domestic supply chain offers resilience where imports are uncertain. Building it may require accepting a slower route to more efficient production.

nodes.label: Train the Managers
nodes.description: Managers and technicians need opportunities to learn beyond the routines of command allocation. Invest in the skills required to operate the new productive arrangements.

nodes.label: Spare Parts Workshops
nodes.description: A machine awaiting a minor imported component is a factory unable to work. Support local repair and spare parts workshops where domestic production is practical.

nodes.label: Results before Targets
nodes.description: The plan should be judged by what reaches households and workshops. Keep the gains of successful experiments while funding the services needed to sustain them.

nodes.label: A Real Front Mandate
nodes.description: An autonomous Fatherland Front government would require a new political settlement. Give its constituent organisations a real mandate rather than treating their consultation as an endorsement already secured.

nodes.label: Workplace Councils
nodes.description: Workplace councils can give producers a direct voice in the conditions of production. Their authority may complicate demands for uniform output.

nodes.label: A Technical Cabinet
nodes.description: A technical cabinet can organise policy around practical expertise. Its work still requires an administration capable of carrying decisions beyond the capital.

nodes.label: Recallable Delegates
nodes.description: Delegates who can be recalled must answer more frequently to their communities. That responsiveness changes the relationship between local representatives and the executive.

nodes.label: Publish the Accounts
nodes.description: Public accounts make it harder to conceal the cost of a policy. Publication also exposes the government to challenges that closed administration can avoid.

nodes.label: An Agrarian Compact
nodes.description: The rural economy needs a compact that producers can regard as legitimate. Negotiate the relationship between procurement, household effort and public support.

nodes.label: Voluntary Cooperatives
nodes.description: Cooperative federations can pool resources without imposing one organisation on every village. Voluntary coordination demands patient administration.

nodes.label: Family Holdings
nodes.description: Protected family holdings offer households greater security over their work. They narrow the space for officials to treat all rural activity as a planning instruction.

nodes.label: Village Clinics
nodes.description: Village clinics turn a promise of social citizenship into a service people can use. Maintaining them requires staff, supplies and a recurring public commitment.

nodes.label: Small Producer Credit
nodes.description: Small producers often lack the working capital to make use of their skills. Provide access to credit while accepting the task of supervising it responsibly.

nodes.label: Socialist Independence
nodes.description: An independent socialist diplomacy must preserve relationships without becoming dependent on a single camp. That freedom carries costs where established channels are easier to use.

nodes.label: Reconcile the Left
nodes.description: The socialist tradition contains voices that the existing order has excluded. Seek reconciliation with dissenters while accepting the political uncertainty of their return.

nodes.label: A Unified Vanguard
nodes.description: The Front can instead become a unified vanguard in its own right. Concentrating authority may preserve direction while limiting independent criticism.

nodes.label: Believers as Citizens
nodes.description: Religious belief should not place a citizen outside the national compact. Translate accommodation into equal treatment by local institutions.

nodes.label: Common Cadre Service
nodes.description: A common cadre service can hold the Front's different organisations together. Its scope must be supported by the administrative resources it demands.

nodes.label: A National Compact
nodes.description: A socialist national compact must reconcile participation with the obligations of government. Its stability depends on sustaining the services promised in its name.

nodes.label: A Constitutional Pact
nodes.description: An independent Democratic Party government would break with its historical role inside the communist led Front. Build a constitutional compact capable of giving that change a legitimate foundation.

nodes.label: Independent Courts
nodes.description: Courts must be able to judge the use of public power without awaiting political permission. Independence requires institutions that can withstand pressure from the executive.

nodes.label: Emergency Executive
nodes.description: An emergency executive offers a more concentrated response to disorder. Its powers place the promised constitutional settlement under strain from the beginning.

nodes.label: Speech and Association
nodes.description: Speech and association make public disagreement a protected part of political life. That opening will also make the government less able to dictate the terms of debate.

nodes.label: A Limited Emergency
nodes.description: Emergency powers need a defined purpose and a credible review. Without limits, temporary authority can become the normal condition of the republic.

nodes.label: A Mixed Economy
nodes.description: Neither unrestricted private control nor comprehensive command offers an easy answer to recovery. Negotiate a mixed economy with public obligations and room for enterprise.

nodes.label: Open Public Tenders
nodes.description: Open tenders can make public contracts answer to more than political connections. Transparency also removes instruments on which an executive may have relied.

nodes.label: National Enterprises
nodes.description: National enterprises can preserve domestic control over important production. Protecting them may come at the expense of wider economic efficiency.

nodes.label: Small Business Rights
nodes.description: Small firms need secure rights before they can plan beyond immediate survival. Establish a legal framework capable of protecting those rights consistently.

nodes.label: A Technical College
nodes.description: A public technical college can widen access to the skills reconstruction requires. It will need a reliable education budget as well as buildings and instructors.

nodes.label: Reconcile the Citizens
nodes.description: Citizens with different wartime loyalties must be able to live under the same civil order. Reconciliation cannot depend on permanent exclusion from public life.

nodes.label: Western Guarantees
nodes.description: Western guarantees might strengthen the government's international position. They also raise difficult questions about dependence and the conditions attached to outside support.

nodes.label: Armed Neutrality
nodes.description: Constitutional government need not commit the republic to a strategic camp. A policy of armed neutrality demands a credible domestic basis for independence.

nodes.label: Trade before Alignment
nodes.description: Trade can develop before a final strategic alignment is settled. Make practical economic contact possible without promising that outside governments will agree to every request.

nodes.label: A Civilian Coalition
nodes.description: A broad civilian coalition can protect constitutional government from a narrow factional contest. Its compromises will make executive decisions slower and more contested.

nodes.label: Government by Consent
nodes.description: Government by consent depends on rules that remain credible when the incumbent loses. Negotiate guarantees that make peaceful political competition possible.

nodes.label: Socialism by Consent
nodes.description: The northern Socialist Party would need a new mandate to govern independently of the Front's historical arrangements. Base that mandate on consent, public service and the rights of organised labour.

nodes.label: Independent Unions
nodes.description: Independent unions can speak for workers beyond the priorities of a ministry or enterprise director. Their bargaining strength may challenge established production arrangements.

nodes.label: A Production Pact
nodes.description: A pact between labour, management and the state can coordinate recovery. It requires institutions capable of mediating interests that do not naturally coincide.

nodes.label: Collective Bargaining
nodes.description: Collective bargaining gives working conditions a place at the negotiating table. The process can protect social peace while slowing some adjustments in production.

nodes.label: Labour Arbitration
nodes.description: Public arbitration offers a way to resolve labour disputes without suppressing them. A fair system requires expertise, time and a trusted administration.

nodes.label: Science in Public Life
nodes.description: Scientists and teachers belong at the centre of public reconstruction. Give their institutions resources adequate to the ambitions placed upon them.

nodes.label: Basic Services for All
nodes.description: Universal basic services can give social citizenship a meaning beyond income. Their continuing cost must be carried honestly in the public budget.

nodes.label: Target Rural Poverty
nodes.description: Targeted provision can reach the poorest districts with fewer resources. It asks the state to identify needs and maintain access without turning assistance into patronage.

nodes.label: Housing Cooperatives
nodes.description: Housing cooperatives can combine public support with the organisation of residents. Their work remains a long term responsibility rather than a single construction announcement.

nodes.label: Health and Literacy
nodes.description: Rural health and literacy can widen the social foundations of recovery. Fund the local institutions that must deliver them through difficult conditions.

nodes.label: A Social Budget
nodes.description: A social budget should show both the promises of government and the means available to honour them. Expose waste without hiding the real cost of public services.

nodes.label: Public Key Industries
nodes.description: Public ownership can preserve control over industries considered essential to national development. It does not remove the problems of management and productive efficiency.

nodes.label: A Cooperative Economy
nodes.description: A cooperative mixed economy can combine social ownership with a wider range of initiative. Its diversity requires a more capable framework of coordination.

nodes.label: Planning Boards
nodes.description: Planning boards can bring elected representatives and producers into economic decisions. Their legitimacy depends on doing useful work rather than multiplying offices.

nodes.label: Firms and Cooperatives
nodes.description: Small firms can coexist with cooperatives where their different strengths meet real demand. Wider exchange will also transmit more movement from the market.

nodes.label: A Social Settlement
nodes.description: A parliamentary social settlement must allow disagreement without abandoning public obligations. Its durability will be measured by how those obligations survive a change of government.

nodes.label: A Republican Mandate
nodes.description: A VNQDD return to Hanoi would require a profound political rupture or a negotiated return from exile. Seek a republican mandate without pretending that nationalist factions have already become one movement.

nodes.label: Constitutional Rule
nodes.description: The constitution should bind the president as firmly as it binds a political opponent. Establish legal limits that cannot be removed whenever the executive finds them inconvenient.

nodes.label: A Strong Presidency
nodes.description: A strong presidency can impose direction on a divided nationalist coalition. That concentration of authority risks weakening the civil institutions the republic claims to defend.

nodes.label: National Reconciliation
nodes.description: National reconciliation requires terms on which former opponents can return to civil life. Offer conditional protection without erasing the memory of the conflict.

nodes.label: Integrate the Factions
nodes.description: Rival armed factions cannot indefinitely remain governments within the government. Bring their integration under common authority while accepting the instability of the process.

nodes.label: Peasant Smallholdings
nodes.description: Secure peasant holdings can give the republic a stronger rural foundation. A practical system of titles and dispute resolution must support that promise.

nodes.label: Protect Local Industry
nodes.description: Protection can help domestic industry survive uncertain conditions. It can also shelter inefficient production and restrict access to more competitive suppliers.

nodes.label: A Commercial Republic
nodes.description: A commercial republic would place more of recovery in the circulation of goods and enterprise. Its opportunities will depend increasingly on conditions beyond national control.

nodes.label: A National Arsenal
nodes.description: A national arsenal can reduce dependence on foreign military supply. Preparing its construction commits scarce capital to defence rather than civilian recovery.

nodes.label: Haiphong Trading House
nodes.description: Haiphong can serve as a centre for legitimate trade and commercial administration. Organise the institutions and construction required to make that role productive.

nodes.label: Equal Citizenship
nodes.description: Religion, region and former allegiance must not determine who belongs to the republic. Turn the language of national unity into equal civil treatment.

nodes.label: No Foreign Tutelage
nodes.description: Independence should not become a change from one foreign patron to another. Preserve room for national decision even where doing so limits easier economic opportunities.

nodes.label: External Guarantees
nodes.description: External guarantees can support a vulnerable republic. Negotiate their terms rather than assuming that outside powers share every Vietnamese objective.

nodes.label: Citizen Defence
nodes.description: Citizen defence can connect sovereignty to a wider social responsibility. It also draws time and resources away from civil reconstruction.

nodes.label: Trade for Development
nodes.description: Trade offers a route to development that military mobilisation cannot supply. Give commercial administration a stable place in national policy.

nodes.label: Beyond Faction
nodes.description: The republic must become more durable than the coalition that brought it to power. Seek institutions capable of surviving factional defeat without another rupture.

nodes.label: The Military Council
nodes.description: A provisional military council would replace the historical relationship between Party and army with a new concentration of power. Its first decisions must determine what the emergency is meant to achieve.
